payload.rationale: Gasoline prices have surged in the first half of September 2026, from roughly $4.20/gal at the end of August to $4.455/gal by mid-September. Furthermore, historical data indicates a strong positive seasonal adjustment factor for gasoline in September (typically adding ~2% to the NSA change). Given gasoline's 3.77% weight, this combination is highly likely to contribute significantly to the headline CPI. Even with moderate core inflation (around 0.2%), the headline SA CPI is strongly positioned to exceed 0.2% (i.e., round to 0.3% or higher).
limitations: Gasoline prices for the second half of September are unknown and could retrace sharply.
Core inflation components (like shelter or used cars) could surprise to the downside, dragging the headline figure lower.
Seasonal adjustment factors are subject to revision and might differ slightly from historical averages.

scenarios.description: September average gasoline prices remain elevated above $4.35/gal.
scenarios.rationale: If gasoline prices maintain their mid-month surge, the NSA increase will be around 4-5%. With a ~2% positive seasonal adjustment, SA gasoline would rise 6-7%, contributing over 0.2% to the headline CPI alone. Combined with a typical core increase, headline CPI will almost certainly be 0.3% or 0.4%.
unknowns: Exact trajectory of retail gasoline prices in late September.

scenarios.description: September average gasoline prices retrace moderately to between $4.25 and $4.35/gal.
scenarios.rationale: A moderate retracement still leaves NSA gasoline prices up 1-3% for the month. The positive seasonal adjustment would push the SA increase to 3-5%, contributing 0.1% to 0.2% to the headline. Assuming core inflation remains near 0.2%, the headline figure is still very likely to round to 0.3%.
unknowns: The extent of the late-month gasoline price drop.

scenarios.description: September average gasoline prices drop sharply below $4.25/gal, or core inflation is unusually weak.
scenarios.rationale: If gasoline prices crash in the second half of the month, the NSA average might be flat or negative. Even with the positive seasonal adjustment, the contribution would be minimal. If core inflation also prints softly (e.g., 0.1%), the headline CPI could easily round to 0.2% or lower.
unknowns: Potential for a sudden collapse in energy markets.
Unexpected downside surprises in shelter or services.

payload.partition_justification: The scenarios are partitioned based on the average retail gasoline price for September, which is the most volatile and currently observable high-impact driver for the month's CPI. The thresholds (>$4.35, $4.25-$4.35, <$4.25) are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive, covering the range of plausible outcomes given the mid-month price of $4.455.

fixtures.success_criterion: Detect weak core overlapping the high or moderate gasoline scenarios (an overlap); identify both matching IDs and a concrete case.

payload.rationale: The forecast depends heavily on the trajectory of gasoline prices in the latter half of September and the stickiness of core inflation. Early September EIA data shows a sharp increase in gasoline prices (from $4.207 on Aug 31 to $4.455 on Sep 14). Given gasoline's 3.77% weight and positive seasonal adjustment factors typically seen in September, energy is poised to contribute significantly to the headline CPI. Core inflation has also been running around 0.2%-0.3%. To fall to 0.2% or below (rounded), we would need a sharp reversal in energy prices in late September combined with very soft core inflation.
limitations: Gasoline prices for the second half of September are unknown.
Core inflation components (like shelter and used cars) can be volatile and are not tracked in real-time here.
Seasonal adjustment factors for 2026 are estimates based on historical patterns and subject to revision.

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices maintain their early September gains or rise further, and core inflation remains at or above 0.2%.
scenarios.rationale: With gasoline prices up significantly in the first two weeks of September, a sustained high price level will result in a strong positive energy contribution. Combined with normal core inflation, headline CPI will easily exceed the 0.2% threshold (likely printing 0.4% or 0.5%).

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices retrace significantly in the second half of September, muting the energy contribution, but core inflation remains steady around 0.2%-0.3%.
scenarios.rationale: If energy prices fall back, the energy contribution will be smaller, but positive seasonal adjustments for September gasoline and a steady core CPI still make a >0.2% print (i.e., 0.3% rounded) the most likely outcome, though with less certainty.
unknowns: Magnitude of the energy price retracement
Exact seasonal adjustment factor for September 2026

scenarios.description: Core inflation unexpectedly drops (0.1% or lower) and energy prices weaken in late September.
scenarios.rationale: A combination of a sharp drop in gasoline prices wiping out early-month gains and a surprisingly soft core inflation print would be required to bring the headline CPI down to 0.2% or lower. This is unlikely given recent trends but possible.
unknowns: Unexpected shocks to travel or medical services

payload.partition_justification: The scenarios are partitioned based on the two primary drivers of the September CPI: the final monthly average of energy prices (given the known early-month spike) and the stickiness of core inflation. They cover the most likely case (energy stays high, core normal), a moderate case (energy retraces, core normal), and a tail risk case (both soften significantly).

fixtures.success_criterion: Detect missing high energy with soft core (a gap); identify scenario IDs and a concrete unmatched case.

assessment_contracts.judgment: Return exactly ONE JSON object, starting with { and ending with }. No Markdown fences, schema, commentary, or extra keys. All probabilities and weights are numbers in [0,1]. Evidence references are objects with exactly packet_id and record_id strings from the supplied references. Required keys: method ("judgment"), rationale (string), limitations (array of strings), evidence_refs (array). Also include probability (number). No other keys.
assessment_contracts.scenario_mixture: Return exactly ONE JSON object, starting with { and ending with }. No Markdown fences, schema, commentary, or extra keys. All probabilities and weights are numbers in [0,1]. Evidence references are objects with exactly packet_id and record_id strings from the supplied references. Required keys: method ("scenario_mixture"), rationale (string), limitations (array of strings), evidence_refs (array). Also include partition_justification (string) and scenarios (array of 3 to 5 objects). Each scenario has exactly id (unique string), description (string), weight (number), probability (number conditional on the scenario), rationale (string), evidence_refs (array), unknowns (array of strings). Weights sum to one. Omit top-level probability; the package computes the weighted sum. No other keys.

review_contract: Return exactly ONE JSON object, starting with { and ending with }. No Markdown fences, schema, commentary, or extra keys. All probabilities and weights are numbers in [0,1]. Evidence references are objects with exactly packet_id and record_id strings from the supplied references. Required keys: decision ("retain" or "revise"), rationale (string), objections (array of objects with exactly direction, objection, response; direction is "too_high" or "too_low"; include both directions), evidence_refs (array). If decision is revise, also include probability (number). If retain, omit probability. No other keys. Explain partition checks inside rationale, not in a new field.
review_instruction:
Audit the supplied scenario partition before assessing its probability.
Read scenario descriptions as logical conditions, including AND/OR clauses.
Identify their underlying dimensions; test combinations across those dimensions,
intermediate cases, exact numerical boundaries, and unspecified conditions.
In your rationale, give concrete witness cases and the IDs of every scenario
each case satisfies. Zero matches means a gap; multiple matches means overlap.
Do not infer that weights summing to one establishes a valid partition. Distinguish
ambiguous wording from a definite gap or overlap. If you find none, show boundary
and combination checks supporting that conclusion. Then challenge the probability
in both directions. Retain it or revise it as an explicit holistic judgment; a
changed probability is NOT a repaired scenario mixture. No new research is available.
Keep the rationale under 450 words and each objection and response under 100 words.
design: Six fresh assessments; three independent partition-review calls if scenario assessments pass; two separate known-flaw diagnostic reviews. Maximum eleven initial calls, no repair or retry of invalid responses.
endpoints: Strict JSON/schema and workflow acceptance by stage, with every failed attempt and cost retained.
Scenario pre/post-review probabilities and qualitative partition checks.
Manual fixture success against the preregistered concrete witness rubric; rubric withheld from reviewers.
cost_limit: At most $2 per trial and $2 per fixture in post-call accounting, not a provider-enforced spending cap.
limitations: Unresolved single question, three repetitions, no accuracy conclusion.
Contract changes are compared descriptively with the earlier pilot, not a randomized concurrent formatting control.
Review sees the initial estimate; this is not an independent blind forecast. A revision is holistic judgment, not a corrected mixture.
Known-flaw fixtures are selected after inspecting the first pilot, include one format-normalized rejected response, and are not forecasts or a representative detection benchmark.
The coordinator knows the old forecasts and defects; fresh forecasters receive no old forecasts. Reviewers receive no defect rubric.
